# How to Build a Quiz in Google Forms with Gemini (What It Can and Can't Do)

> **In short:** Google Forms now has a "Help me create" button powered by Gemini. You describe the quiz you want in a sentence, and Forms drafts questions and answer choices for you. The feature works in any modern browser on a personal Google account or Google Workspace, though the exact rollout is still in progress.

It's Sunday evening, you promised a quiz for tomorrow's class, and the textbook chapter is 40 pages long. Or you're a trainer with a workshop next week and you need a quick knowledge check on safety procedures. Making a quiz from scratch — finding the right questions, setting the correct answer, choosing the right format — usually takes 20 to 30 minutes of fiddling about.

Now there's a faster way. Google's Gemini AI (the same general-purpose assistant that powers many of Google's tools) is built right into Google Forms under a "Help me create" feature. You describe what you want in plain English, and Forms drafts a quiz for you. Here's what to expect — and where the limits still are.

## What "Help me create" actually does

When you open a new form in Google Forms, you'll see a **"Help me create"** button. Clicking it opens a small side panel where you type a description of the quiz you want. Gemini then drafts questions and answer choices directly into your form.

The feature works best when your **prompt** (the instruction you give to an AI) is specific. A clear brief — topic, year level, number of questions, difficulty — produces a much better draft than a vague one. Think of it like briefing a new colleague: the more context you give, the less editing you'll do afterwards.

**What it does well today:**

- Drafts multiple-choice, checkbox, and short-answer questions on a wide range of topics
- Marks a suggested correct answer for each question
- Mixes difficulty levels when you ask it to
- Generates a full quiz in under a minute

## What it doesn't do (yet)

Here's the honest part. The current "Help me create" panel does **not** let you attach a Google Doc, Slide, or PDF from your Drive as a source for the questions. It works from general knowledge, not from your own files. So if you want questions drawn from a specific textbook chapter or a slide deck you've written, you'll need to paste the relevant text into the prompt itself, or write the questions manually.

This is the single biggest limitation to know about. A few other small things to be aware of:

- Gemini doesn't always set the question type you want. It defaults to multiple choice, but you can change any question's **type** (multiple choice, checkboxes, short answer, dropdown) using the dropdown on the bottom-right of each question after insertion.
- It can mark a wrong answer as correct. This is a **hallucination** (when an AI confidently makes something up), and even Gemini does it occasionally. Always review.
- It's rolling out gradually through 2026. If you don't see the button yet, give it a few days.

## How to get a good result

Because you can't upload source files, the trick is to **paste the key information into your prompt** instead. If you've got a chapter summary in a Doc, copy the most important paragraphs into the "Help me create" box along with your instructions.

💬 **Example prompt:**
*Based on the following notes about the water cycle — evaporation, condensation, precipitation, collection — create an 8-question multiple-choice quiz for Year 4 students. Mix easy and harder questions. Mark the correct answer for each one.*

The more relevant text you include, the closer the questions will be to what you actually want to teach. After insertion, take two minutes to:

- Spot-check every correct answer
- Rewrite any question that's awkwardly worded
- Delete any question that doesn't fit your lesson
- Tweak the marked answer if Gemini got it wrong

## Turning it into a proper quiz

Once the draft is in your form, head to the **Settings** tab (the cog icon at the top) and turn on **"Make this a quiz"** if it isn't already. This is what unlocks automatic marking and the correct-answer fields.

After that, you can:

- Toggle **"Required question"** on or off for each question
- Re-order questions by dragging the six-dot handle on the right
- Click **Preview** (the eye icon, top-right) to test the quiz yourself before sharing

To share it, click **Send** (top-right) and choose email, a shortened link, or Google Classroom if you teach in a school.

## What this means for you

- **If you're a teacher or trainer:** This can cut your quiz-making time in half for general knowledge topics. The trick is to write a clear brief and treat the draft as a starting point — your professional judgement is still what makes the quiz good. For curriculum-specific questions, paste the relevant text into the prompt.
- **If you run a small business or community group:** Use it for quick knowledge checks — workplace safety refreshers, onboarding quizzes, volunteer training. You don't need to be a quiz expert; describe the topic and let Gemini handle the structure.
- **If you're a student or self-learner:** Paste your revision notes into the prompt and ask Gemini to quiz you on them. It's a surprisingly effective study tool, and you can regenerate fresh questions any time.

## Wrap-up

Gemini in Google Forms is genuinely useful for general-knowledge quizzes, and the drafts are usually good enough to edit rather than write from scratch. The honest limitation is that it doesn't yet read your uploaded files — so for now, paste the source text directly into your prompt. Try it once: open Forms, click **"Help me create"**, and type a sentence about any topic you know well. Once you've seen the draft appear, you'll find plenty of excuses to use it again.
